insights.insight: The protocol has produced 8,585 cryptographically verified purchase receipts — each one confirming a transaction occurred, not inferring it might. At a cost of ~$0.10 per verified receipt versus $5–$150 CPA in probabilistic ad tech, the structural cost delta is 50–200x, not a rounding error.

The 7-day rolling GMV window has oscillated between $92K and $99K in recent cycles, with 35% of all-time GMV ($225K of $639K) accumulated in the trailing 14 days — meaning the network's recent throughput now outweighs its entire prior history combined.

A single 4-hour cycle on April 6 added $55,679 in GMV at an implied $1,031 per receipt — driven by retail and department stores — and the elevated average ticket (~$177) has held across subsequent cycles, signaling a durable shift in buyer composition, not a one-time spike.

The April 6 heartbeat recorded 22 new CBSAs entering the signal window in a single cycle — the highest single-heartbeat count on record — with coverage explicitly extending into rural and non-metro markets across AZ, FL, IA, HI, WI, MO, and KS, not just deepening within existing urban clusters.

insights.topic: Brand coverage spanning the full retail stack
insights.insight: Brands rotating through the top receipt list include Walmart, Amazon, CVS, Target, Best Buy, Whole Foods, Dollar General, BJ's Wholesale Club, Etsy, and Depop — confirming signal coverage across grocery, big-box, specialty, discount, warehouse, and peer-to-peer resale, with no single vertical dominating.

insights.topic: Rolling-window artifact risk for measurement teams
insights.insight: Two separate cycles showed the 7-day GMV window drop while cumulative GMV continued rising — a mechanical result of high-value receipts aging out of the window, not a reversal in throughput. Measurement teams using windowed metrics on this data need to account for this artifact before drawing trend conclusions.
